rule: A pitch must name the show's own date, in the subject or the body, and must never name a different one (#2864). Shared by DraftEventDateCasesTests (Swift, EventDateInDraft) and draftEventDateCases.test.ts (TypeScript, prepEval.eventDateVerdict). The Swift side is the source of truth: it is what runs on Dan's screen.

cases.name: body names the date
cases.body: I'd love to photograph your March 10 concert.

cases.name: bare ordinal with the month in the same sentence
cases.body: Your March programme, and specifically the 10th, is what I'm writing about.

cases.name: upper case
cases.body: MARCH 10 is the night I have in mind.

cases.name: the subject alone carries it
cases.subject: Photographing your March 10 concert
cases.body: Nothing dated in here at all.

cases.name: a real compliant cold draft
cases.subject: Photographing Lumen Dance's March 12 performance at the Grand Theatre
cases.body: My name is Dan and I'm a professional arts photographer here in NYC. I saw that Downtown Presents is bringing Lumen Dance to the Grand Theatre on March 12. I shoot unobtrusive documentary coverage without flash, my rate is $250 an hour plus tax, and I deliver the gallery within two weeks. What are your photography plans for this one?

cases.name: no date anywhere
cases.body: I'd love to photograph your concert. My rate is $250 an hour plus tax.

cases.name: a rate and a delivery window are not a date
cases.body: My rate is $250 an hour plus tax and I deliver within two weeks.

cases.name: a different day
cases.body: I'd love to photograph your concert on March 3.

cases.name: the shape of the pitch that was sent
cases.body: ...the chance to photograph your company's programme at the theater on July 18, working quietly from the back of house.

cases.name: the right day in the wrong year
a run named by its span
a run named by a hyphenated span
a span whose only acceptable nights are inside it
a span that ends before the run does
an opening night that has already gone
a still upcoming night of an opened run
a run wholly in the past accepts any of its own nights
